theory.intro: A **hemisphere** is exactly half a sphere, so its volume is half the sphere formula: $V = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$.
facts: **$V = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$**, where $r$ is the radius.
Find the whole sphere's volume and halve it, or use $\frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$ straight away.
Use the **radius**; halve a given diameter first.
Round only at the last line, to the form the question asks for.
steps: Substitute the radius, halving a diameter first

workedExamples.solution_text:
A hemisphere has half the volume of a sphere.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\times\pi\times4.5^{3}\\&=60.75\pi\\&\approx190.85\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Halve the diameter to find the radius.
$r=\frac{13}{2}=6.5\text{ cm}$
$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\times\pi\times6.5^{3}\\&=\frac{2197\pi}{12}\\&\approx575\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A hemispherical bowl has radius $7.5$ cm. Sam uses $V=\frac{4}{3}\pi\times7.5^{3}$ to calculate its volume. Explain the mistake and find the correct volume to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Sam used the whole-sphere formula. A hemisphere is half a sphere, so halve that volume.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{3}\times\pi\times7.5^{3}\\&=281.25\pi\\&\approx883.57\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$
